en: Oṃ! The one whose form is consciousness, the Sustainer, the bestower of supreme bliss, whose body is purifying,

who is to be constantly served by the lords of sages, the lords of yogis, the lords of ascetics, the lords of gods, and by Hanumān— the perfect one, the preceptor of the gods, whose limbs are the daughter of Janaka.
May Rāma, the lord of Ramā, ever delight in my heart. || 1 ||
Mukunda, Govinda, whose feet are caressed by the daughter of Janaka— he, from whom even Śabarī, though born of a lowly family, attained his abode;
he who is beyond speech and inaccessible even to those of pure intellect through the words of the Vedas.
May Rāma, the Lord of Ramā, ever delight within my heart. || 2 ||
The lord of the earth, sovereign of gods and eminent men, the Lord of the Raghus—
wearing a crown and armlets, his body golden-hued and radiant—
sat upon a throne resembling a hundred suns, with a tranquil mind.
May Rāma, the Lord of Ramā, ever delight within my heart. || 3 ||

The most excellent one, the refuge, the friend of the lord of monkeys, whose inner distress has ceased, who is red as saffron upon his forehead, whose gait and form are beautiful, whose face is like the moon,
who is Rāma in human form, praised by the lord of ascetics, and the remover of the cycle of worldly existence— [to him I bow].
May Rāma, the Lord of Ramā, ever delight within my heart. || 4 ||
In Kāśī, Virūpākṣa teaches that thousand-name hymn which bestows auspiciousness,
the recitation of which at dawn by Girijā causes the deeds of that Lord to be sung in his own world by the faces of Īśvara and the other deities.
May Rāma, the Lord of Ramā, ever delight in my heart. || 5 ||
The supreme, steadfast one; the unsteady one; born of the lineage of Asuras and yet the destroyer of Asuras;
the Supreme Self; the omniscient one whose excellent fame is sung by hosts of men and gods;
the destroyer of Ahalyā’s curse; the one who made Śara straight; the friend of Kauśika.
May Rāmānātha, the Delightful One, ever delight within my heart. || 6 ||
May Hṛṣīkeśa, Śauri, the one who reclines upon the supporter of the earth, Madhuripu,
Upendra, Vaikuṇṭha, Gajaripuhara, Balidhvaṃsī, the Hero, and the son of Daśaratha, who is skilled in ethics, be pleased in his mind.
May Rāma, the lord of Ramā, ever delight in my heart. || 7 ||
A poet, worthy of praise by the son of Sumitrā, slayer of the deceptive deer, forest-dweller,
one who delights in battle, self-controlled, remover of the earth's burden, praised by the gods,
free from pride yet cognizant of honor, worshiped by all people, and the one who dwells within the heart.
May Rāmānātha, the Delightful One, ever delight in my heart. || 8 ||
If a person recites this excellent *Rāmastotra*, composed by Amaradāsa, with devotion and full of spiritual feeling at the hour of dawn,
he shall quickly [overcome] the fear of birth and death that produces suffering.
Having abandoned the most auspicious state of being the Lord of the Raghus, he goes to that which bestows [only] worldly welfare.
Thus ends the *Śrīrāmacandrāṣṭaka*, composed by the poet named Amara Dāsa, disciple of Śrīmat Haṃsadāsa, who was himself a disciple of the venerable feet of Śrīmad Rāmadāsa.
